steps.title: Nine sides
steps.text: Chicagoans place a neighbourhood by its side of town: the North Side, the South Side, the West Side and six more, with Central around the Loop. Ask someone where they live and the side often comes first.

steps.title: 77 community areas
steps.text: Within the sides are 77 official community areas, first drawn in the 1920s and still used for city statistics. The names in italics are the neighbourhoods people actually say, like Wicker Park, Pilsen or Wrigleyville.

steps.title: The address grid
steps.text: Chicago's addresses are a grid. State and Madison, in the Loop, are 0, and numbers count out from there, 800 to a mile: 2400 N is three miles north, and 1600 W is Ashland. Tap any spot and the card gives its numbers.

steps.title: Getting around
steps.text: The 'L' is named for its elevated tracks, and its lines meet around the Loop, the ring of track downtown. Metra commuter trains run from downtown stations out to the suburbs.

steps.title: Tap anywhere
steps.text: Tap any spot or search an address, and the card shows the boundaries it falls in, what living there is like, transit nearby and who represents it. Compare puts two places side by side. Switch layers on and off in the panel to explore.

address.label: Address grid
address.sub: State and Madison are 0; a mile is 800 numbers (1,200 for the first mile south of Madison).

lang.label: Language at home
lang.note: English only, or the language besides English that each person 5 or older speaks at home. For small areas the Census groups some languages: Polish shares a group with Russian and other Slavic languages.

recent.caveat: Share of residents, from the 2020–2024 survey. Toronto counts a shorter window (2016–21), so the two cities don't compare directly.

schools.title: Schools
schools.note: The Chicago Public Schools whose attendance area this spot is in, from CPS’s {year} boundaries. Distances are straight-line to the school building. Boundaries change; CPS’s school locator has the final word.

transit.title: Transit nearby
transit.every: about every {h} min on weekday middays
transit.note: Routes with a stop within ¼ mile, about a 5-minute walk. Filled numbers come every 10 minutes or better on weekdays. Tap a number to draw the route. CTA schedules, week of {week}.

nearby.note: Straight-line distances; half a mile is about a 10-minute walk. Chicago Public Library, the ERs layer and the Park District and City community centers, and OpenStreetMap (parks, playgrounds, courts).

trustees.note: School board candidates are from the Chicago Board of Elections’ candidate list, and counts from its results pages; results are unofficial until the board proclaims them.

reps.note: Names open each person’s official page. Chicago’s city council elections are nonpartisan. Checked weekly against those sources; last change {date}.
